AgentHostIpcChannels.RemoteProxy.why: patch 0015 gates the agent-host transport by wrapping this channel inside EditorRemoteAgentHostServiceClient, so every caller that instantiates that client is gated (including patch 0010's selection in agentHostService.ts). A second renderer-side consumer would bypass the gate entirely, and no runtime probe can show that none exists.

ExtHostContext.ExtHostDocumentsAndEditor.why: patch 0035 filters which text models reach a tab extension host inside MainThreadDocumentsAndEditors. A second window-side holder of this proxy could push host documents past the filter, and no runtime probe can show that none exists.

ExtHostContext.ExtHostDocuments).why: patch 0035: model content changes and dirty, save and encoding events reach a tab only through MainThreadDocuments, whose ModelTracker and file events apply the same provenance filter. A second window-side getProxy of this shape would bypass it.

__upstreamInvariants.why: facts about upstream that a patch's security argument depends on, which no unit test can hold because the unit container has no upstream checkout. Checked over the patched tree by build/check-sole-consumer.ts, which patch-build already runs.

rules.why: patch 0017 pins workbench.browser.dataStorage to 'ephemeral' precisely because upstream drops the browser view's network for the global scope and keeps it for ephemeral. If either branch changes, the pinned value must be re-derived before it can still be trusted.

rules.why: the browser TOOL supplies its own session scope, so `workbench.browser.dataStorage` is never consulted on the agent-tool path at all: `_resolveSessionRequest` returns a request verbatim when it already carries a scope. The U-vs-F proof therefore measures that key on the non-agent create path (a restored editor, a user-opened view), and no claim about the browser tool may be drawn from it. Recorded because this is the whole reason the dataStorage half is pinned by source reading rather than by the tool probe (security review rounds 8 and 9, finding `the dataStorage half is never exercised`). If upstream stops supplying a scope here, the tool path starts reading the setting and the probe's scope becomes the stronger evidence -- a change we must notice.

the early return is what makes the invariant above load-bearing: a session request that already carries a scope is returned verbatim, WITHOUT reading `workbench.browser.dataStorage`. Patch 0017 also relies on the configured-storage branch still existing and still reading that exact setting id, since the patch fixes the value the window reads there. If either half changes, the 0017 security argument and the increment 2 proof both need rereading.
